# Catan engine progress and pause handoff

Work paused at the user's request on 12 September 2026 at 02:01 UTC (03:01 London). The scheduled heartbeat is paused and all tournament workers have stopped. Engine **0.4.0 / Tactical v4** remains the tested default. No further engine changes were started during the final checkpoint save.

## What is working

The browser and native runner use the same Python rules engine. It plays complete four-player games and supports replay export/import, undo, policy comparisons and downloadable research. Decisions use only the acting player's observation.

- Initial placements account for production pips, distinct dice outcomes, resource balance, snake draft order, likely remaining sites, starting cards and resource costs. Initial roads are scored for reachable expansion. Ports matter through resource conversion rates and expected time saved, rather than a flat port bonus.
- Resource beliefs track public production, spending and trades, retaining uncertainty after hidden thefts/discards. Hidden development-card estimates now incorporate completed turns and purchase ages. These are explicit models, not access to real hidden cards.
- Turn order and dice exposure inform forecasts. Robber choices consider production denial and stealing; the forecast can estimate modeled winning outcomes through simulated games. Those estimates are not calibrated probabilities against human opponents.
- Tactical play recognizes immediate wins and public road/army award changes. Corrected road rules handle rival settlement endpoints and award ties. Sampled hands respect the finite bank.
- Tactical v4 fixes an observation mismatch: the displayed recommendation used tracked cards while autoplay sometimes fell back to production estimates. All 43 mismatches in the 77-decision Monopoly audit are resolved. In the captured example, the bot now takes eight wheat instead of choosing wood.
- Optimized continuations measured **3.77× faster** across six local positions, with identical decisions and outcomes to the reference. This is a runtime result, not a strength multiplier.

## Completed Tactical v4 measurements

Every batch used fresh boards, all four challenger seats, corrected rules, tracked resources, fixed settings and immutable source snapshots. These are separate opponent populations; do not pool them.

| Three opponents | Wins / games | Win rate | 95% whole-board bootstrap interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Frozen Tactical v3 | 215 / 800 | 26.875% | 25.25–28.50% |
| Frozen strategic v2 | 223 / 800 | 27.875% | 26.00–29.75% |
| Original v1 | 205 / 400 | 51.25% | 46.25–56.00% |

All **2,000 games completed with zero errors or truncations**. The equal-policy reference is 25% in a four-player game. The v3 comparison supports a modest improvement against that specific population; these are not human-strength or equilibrium results. Raw outcomes, seeds, seats, source hashes and uncertainty: [v3 opponents](strength-v4.json), [v2 opponents](strength-v4-v2.json), [v1 opponents](strength-v4-original.json). The [protocol](tactical-v4-protocol.md) was fixed before outcomes.

Validation at the last engine release: **210 native tests, 24 browser checks and six content checks pass**; two desktop-only browser cases are intentionally skipped on mobile. This pause release changes reports, links and saved checkpoints, not engine behavior.

## Search: measured limitations

The optional search samples hidden worlds and runs actual game continuations with UCB allocation at the root. It is not a full equilibrium solver or a trained neural policy.

- Engine 0.3.1, budget 12: **21/100 wins**, versus **26/100** for the matched fast control. Paired difference −5 percentage points; interval −13 to +3. No demonstrated improvement. [Report](search12-v031-comparison.json).
- Engine 0.3.2, budget 12: **12/100 wins**, versus **29/100** for the matched fast control. Paired difference −17 points; interval −26 to −8. Search underperformed on this batch. The changed boards and sampler prevent attributing the difference between releases to one cause. [Report](search12-v032-comparison.json).
- A fixed-position audit found unstable recommendations and optimistic selected scores. Its independent reference rollouts estimate the same imperfect continuation model, not ground truth. [Audit](root-search-audit.md).
- The older budget-48 trial is **paused at 62/100 completed games**, with 15 recorded wins and no recorded errors/truncations. The remaining 38 outcomes are unknown. It is incomplete and supports no final strength conclusion. [Pause report](search48-v031-paused.json).

The [portable checkpoint](checkpoints/search48-v031-5500.zip) includes the frozen 0.3.1 engine, manifest, all completed game records/replays, diagnostics and progress. SHA-256: `a4a3e186ed55812e9a4982df37caab76c8b68d29ee5054607b789e7e882a57d5`.

The original local directory is `../../work/experiments/search48-v031-5500` relative to the repository. For a portable resume, extract the checkpoint into a new experiment directory. Install the engine requirements and run this command **from the extracted `search48-v031-5500/source` directory**, with its parent as the output directory:

```sh
python -m engine.arena --worker-snapshot --challenger search --opponents strategic --boards 25 --seed 5500 --workers 4 --budget 48 --horizon 1600 --candidates 4 --max-actions 4000 --track-beliefs --output ..
```

Do not run this command until the user resumes the work. The runner retains the 62 recorded games and starts the 38 missing games from their seeds; partially played games are restarted, not resumed mid-turn. Use the frozen source and original manifest unchanged. Do not launch duplicate runners. When complete, compare against the existing budget-12 arm and fast control on the same boards with `scripts/compare-arena.py`.

## Next research step, not implemented

Test whether comparing candidate actions with shared sampled hands/deck and shared future dice reduces irrelevant simulation noise. The dice stream should be separate from theft randomness, and no future draws may reach the policy observation. The rules engine's existing roll-result execution hook could support this without changing real-game randomness. Shared randomness helps only when outcomes have positive covariance; it can also hurt. This is a hypothesis based on [Veness, Lanctot and Bowling, 2011](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2011/file/d736bb10d83a904aefc1d6ce93dc54b8-Paper.pdf), not evidence of a Catan improvement.

Preserve the current independent search for comparison. First test marginal chance distributions, conservation, isolation, reproducibility and accounting of every rollout. Then use the existing tuning packets on seeds 6400–6411 (11 eligible positions; 6408 excluded by the fixed rule). Only after that consider fresh, matched full-game trials; seeds 7000 onward remain unused. Keep Tactical v4 as the default unless new evidence supports a change.

No deep reinforcement-learning model has been trained, and mathematically optimal/GTO Catan has not been established. Remaining work includes stronger continuation/value models, more search validation, richer opponent/trading models and outside-game event ingestion.
